title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses measuring similarity between incomplete data without discarding samples or imputing in the original space. It proposes the proximity kernel: equal-frequency binning with proximity (nearest-center) assignment to produce a high-dimensional sparse one-hot representation, plus a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global priors) using kernel mean embedding to encode missing features. On K-means clustering over 12 UCI incomplete datasets it achieves the highest average NMI (0.4245) with linear time complexity.

match_target.why: User hint targets Table 3 proximity kernel NMI on Hepatitis with K-means. It is the paper's central clustering result on one of the smallest datasets (155 samples, 19 features), so it is the cheapest reproduction that still exercises the full method (binning, cascading fallback, kernel representation, K-means).

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded score (NMI in [0,1]) on a small dataset (155 samples, below 2000); no std reported, so band is 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Select nbins bin centers per feature using equal-frequency binning: evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values, with first/last centers equal to min/max.
requirements.quote: The bin centers cj,k are determined by computing evenly-spaced percentiles of the observed distribution

requirements.stmt: Assign each observed value to its nearest bin center (proximity assignment), forming Voronoi cells rather than interval membership.
requirements.quote: we assign each observed value to its nearest center

requirements.stmt: One-hot encode each feature's bin assignment and concatenate across all features into z_i of length d x nbins.
Handle missing features via three-level cascading fallback: intersection matching, then union matching, then global priors.
requirements.quote: we relax to samples matching on any observed feature (union-based matching)

requirements.stmt: Level 1: S1(i) is the intersection over observed features of samples sharing the same bin; estimate missing encoding by averaging matched samples' one-hot vectors (KME).
requirements.quote: we estimate missing encoding through kernel mean embedding

requirements.stmt: Level 2: if S1 is empty, use union S2(i) of samples matching on any observed feature and average their encodings.
requirements.quote: This set contains all samples that share at least one Voronoi cell with sample i in any observed feature

requirements.stmt: Level 3: if S2 is empty, set the missing encoding to the global empirical bin distribution of that feature.
requirements.quote: we cannot leverage local similarity and must use the global distribution of each missing feature

requirements.stmt: Define the proximity kernel as the normalized inner product of encodings, K(xm,xn) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n.
requirements.quote: it computes the expected probability that two samples fall into the same bin, averaged across all features

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with K-means clustering on the kernel representation, with number of clusters equal to ground-truth classes, metric NMI.
requirements.quote: we evaluate all methods on clustering quality using Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) as the metric

requirements.stmt: Tune nbins over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8} and average results over 10 runs.
requirements.quote: we search the number of bins per dimension in {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}
